name: Longleaf Landscape Stewardship Fund
summary: Grants to restore, enhance and conserve longleaf pine and bottomland forest across the historical longleaf range in the southeastern United States, including building local organisations' capacity to lead restoration.

geography.label: Historical longleaf pine range, southeastern United States

reporting: Grantees report on project metrics chosen from the fund's list in NFWF's Easygrants system.

eligibility.rule: Not a U.S. Federal agency, business, unincorporated individual or international organization
The project occurs within the historical longleaf pine range
Capacity-building is part of a larger project addressing strategies 1-4
Conservation acquisitions form part of a broader restoration proposal
No ongoing legal-compliance costs, except improvements beyond baseline compliance

documents: Statement of Litigation, unless a government applicant
Board of Trustees or Directors list, or statement that none exists
GAAP audited financial statements, unless current valid information is already on file
IRS Form 990, unless current valid information is already on file
Single Audit, unless current valid information is already on file
DoD Questionnaire and base commander letter, for projects benefiting a military installation
State Forestry office letter, for projects on state and private lands
National Forest Supervisor letter, for work on a National Forest

status.quote: Longleaf Landscape Stewardship Fund 2026 Request for Proposals - CLOSED

deadline.quote: Full Proposal Due Date January 29, 2026, 11:59 PM, Eastern Time

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal Governments and Organizations, and educational institutions.

geography.quote: expands, enhances and accelerates longleaf pine ecosystem restoration across longleaf pine's historical range throughout the southeastern United States

access.quote: All application materials must be submitted online through National Fish and Wildlife Foundation's Easygrants system.

amount.quote: Grant awards are expected to range from $250,000 to $2,000,000.

co_finance_required.quote: Matching funds are encouraged but not required.

reporting.quote: the Longleaf Landscape Stewardship Fund has a list of metrics in Easygrants for full proposal applicants to choose from for reporting

effort.quote: Full Proposal Due Date January 29, 2026, 11:59 PM, Eastern Time

eligibility.quote: Ineligible applicants include U.S. Federal government agencies, businesses, unincorporated individuals, and international organizations.
Projects must occur within the historical longleaf pine range.
Proposed capacity-building activities must be integrated as part of a larger project addressing one or more of strategies 1-4 above.

Limited funding is available to facilitate voluntary, targeted conservation easement and/or fee-simple acquisition projects that protect existing, high-quality longleaf pine and bottomland forest habitat that are part of a broader restoration proposal.

NFWF funds may not be used to support ongoing efforts to comply with legal requirements, including permit conditions, mitigation and settlement agreements. However, grant funds may be used to support projects that enhance or improve upon existing baseline compliance efforts.

documents.quote: Full Proposal Narrative: The most important upload is your actual full proposal narrative.

Statement of Litigation Yes Template provided in Easygrants online application "Uploads" section. Federal, state, and local government applicants are not required to complete this section. Board of Trustees or Directors Yes Provide a list of members. If your organization is not a nonprofit and does not have a Board, upload a document stating that none exists. GAAP Audited Financial Statements* Yes

IRS Form 990* Yes Please refer to the Required Financial Documents and FAQs webpage for details on all financial information required for submission. Single Audit* Yes Please refer to the Required Financial Documents and FAQs webpage for details on all financial information required for submission. Applicant Controls Questionnaire Yes
Upload the completed and signed DOD questionnaire. Only required for projects involving or benefiting a local military installation or base.

Letter of support from the appropriate military installation/base Commander, or official designee that addresses the specific project benefits to the military mission are required for projects involving or benefitting a local military installation or base.

Letter(s) from the applicable State Forestry office(s), highlighting how the proposed project is being coordinated with their office is required for projects including work on state and private lands.
Letter of support from the Forest Supervisor of the applicable National Forest is required for projects that include work on a National Forest.
